findings.title: com.example.stickerexplode: 31/32 frames janky (96.9%)
findings.detail: Worst frame ran 156 ms over its deadline. App-attributed jank: 12, SurfaceFlinger-attributed: 5.
findings.action: Blame lands on the app. Look at the UI-thread vs RenderThread split and the hot slices during janky frames.

findings.title: 2991 classes loaded during startup, 31 ms on the critical path
findings.detail: startup_id=1 (com.example.stickerexplode). Note this counts explicit class-load slices only; JIT and verification cost sits in the running time above.
findings.action: This is the clearest Baseline Profile signal there is. Generate one with BaselineProfileRule, then prove the win by benchmarking CompilationMode.None() against CompilationMode.Partial(BaselineProfileMode.Require).

findings.title: com.example.stickerexplode: cost is on the UI thread
findings.detail: doFrame 547 ms vs DrawFrame 404 ms (vsync delay 308 ms).
findings.action: Look for measure/layout passes, recomposition, main-thread IO or deserialisation, and work posted onto the main Handler.

findings.title: Measure/layout/traversal cost during janky frames (1316 ms)
findings.action: Flatten the hierarchy, avoid nested weights / double measure, and hoist state so recomposition scopes stay small.

findings.title: Main-thread binder: AIDL::cpp::android.gui.SensorEventConnection::#2::server costs 53 ms
findings.detail: 2 synchronous calls from com.example.stickerexplode to system_server, worst single call 42.5 ms.
findings.action: Synchronous binder on the main thread is a frozen UI. Cache the result, batch the calls, or move them to a background dispatcher. System APIs that look local (PackageManager, ConnectivityManager, DisplayManager, SharedPreferences-backed system settings) are binder calls underneath.

findings.title: App never calls reportFullyDrawn()
findings.detail: com.example.stickerexplode has no time-to-full-display. TTID only measures the first frame, which is often a skeleton or spinner.
findings.action: Call Activity.reportFullyDrawn() (or ReportDrawn* in Compose) once real content is on screen, so TTFD becomes measurable and Play Console reports it.

findings.title: Startup time is dominated by 'choreographer_do_frame'
findings.detail: choreographer_do_frame 93 ms, binder 61 ms, Running 33 ms
findings.action: First-frame rendering is expensive. Usually composition/measure/layout cost or shader compilation.

findings.title: Startup is COMPUTE-bound — main thread runs 66% of the time
findings.detail: Running 172 ms vs waiting 90 ms (Running 172 ms, Sleeping 75 ms, Uninterruptible Sleep (IO) 9 ms, Runnable (Preempted) 3 ms, Runnable 3 ms, Uninterruptible Sleep (non-IO) 0 ms, Uninterruptible Sleep 0 ms).
findings.action: Your code, class loading, or JIT is the cost. Baseline Profiles and deferring init work off the critical path are the levers.

findings.title: Slow binder calls are queueing, not computing
findings.action: The server side is not the bottleneck; the client is descheduled or waiting for a free binder thread. Reducing call *count* helps more than making the server faster.
